annotation.kind: source selection, conventional Cholesky execution certificate, square-root trace, symmetry completion, and zero-based index adapter

assumptions: A is symmetric and belongs to one finite symmetric radix format whose values have bounded radix expansions at the recorded precision and exponent range; rounding is to nearest with unit roundoff u, and membership of the computed upper-triangular factor RHat is a conclusion, not an input premise.

Conventional column-wise Cholesky runs to completion: every off-diagonal entry is linked to its rounded subtraction and pivot-division execution, and every diagonal entry is linked to its rounded subtraction and square-root execution.

Every scalar execution records rounded products, an arbitrary permuted binary summation tree, the protected input's path through actual rounded merges, and range checks excluding underflow and overflow; square-root radicands are nonnegative.

The arithmetic interface exposes the paper's standalone square-root rounding estimate (3.7), while the protected trace assumes only the earlier equation (2.4) sibling estimates. Lemmas 4.1 and 4.3 and all Cholesky bounds must be derived.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P05 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P05 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p05_t3_cholesky_backward_error {n : Nat} (run : P05CholeskyRun n) : RHat is representable, the local (4.5a)-(4.5b) bounds, and exists DeltaA, transpose(RHat)*RHat=A+DeltaA with rowwise (i+2)u and uniform (n+1)u componentwise bounds
formal_statement.plain_language: Every completed range-safe conventional Cholesky execution produces a floating-point factor and has the two distinct local residual estimates and the exact rowwise and uniform componentwise backward-error bounds of Theorem 4.4.

informal_proof: First derive representability of every RHat entry from its rounded quotient or square-root output, using representability of zero below the diagonal. Prove Lemma 4.1 from each off-diagonal protected trace. For each diagonal trace, combine the square-root estimate (3.7) with the protected-tree form of Theorem 3.1 to prove Lemma 4.3. This yields (4.5a) and (4.5b). Upper-triangular support identifies the local sums with entries of transpose(RHat)*RHat. Use symmetry of A, the Gram product, and its absolute majorant to cover the lower triangle; then compare each zero-based row coefficient i+2 with n+1.
informal_statement: Theorem 4.4 in full: the computed floating-point Cholesky factor, its two local estimates, the exact backward relation, and the rowwise and uniform bounds in equation (4.4).

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The frozen library directly supplies symmetry of a generic transpose-self Gram product, which the L proof instantiates for RHat and |RHat|. It has no theorem for P05's scalar Cholesky executions, local coefficients, or full backward-error conclusion.

tier_rationale: The nearby transpose-self Gram symmetry is an elementary matrix fact available from Mathlib-level reasoning and does not materially speed L. Both conditions must develop the rounded division and square-root traces, two local residual families, triangular truncation, perturbation assembly, and row-dependent coefficient bounds.
